evidence.snippet: **The guarantee:** two installs with one digest hold the same manifest and the same link at every place in every `node_modules` tree Node searches beneath the install root, so every import from Melian's code reaches the same release.

verification.reason: The trace holds in `#scan`. `node_modules/@earendil-works` is entered in "scope" mode. For its child `node_modules`, `slot` is true because the mode is "scope" and the name has no leading dot. The `@` branch needs mode "modules", so the child mode is "package". The `entry.name === "node_modules"` branch is never reached, because it only applies when `slot` is false. In "package" mode, `#release` records only `no manifest`, and the children of a package become "tree" (`slot` is false). `openai` is therefore "tree", so its `package.json` is never read or keyed. `#follow`'s ancestors loop only queues a `node_modules` for link targets, so it doesn't catch this. Nothing adds the directory to `#odd`, and `unrecognised(start)` only checks the module's own path. So the digest stays the same and `identified` stays true. Node does search `.../@earendil-works/node_modules` for imports from `@earendil-works/pi-ai`, because only a directory whose basename is exactly `node_modules` is skipped. A swapped hand-made copy would be reused by the lens request key. The decision file's guarantee covers "every place in every node_modules tree Node searches", and it classes this kind of false-identified read as a blocking key defect. I found no test for this layout. The claim's second example, `node_modules/node_modules/yaml`, is not searched by Node, so it is a non-issue. The first example is enough. The layout is rare and hand-made, which fits P2.

AGENTS.md:33 says "TSDoc only on exported package API. Nothing on internals." `PastBound` at installed-packages.ts:18-19 carries a `/** */` block. packages/pipeline/src/index.ts:62 exports only `type Install` and `InstalledPackagesError` from that module. A search of the repo finds no export of `PastBound` there. Only `Install.read` and `Walk` use it, and the type is not reachable from the package API. The repo has earlier rulings of this shape: several comparison records mark TSDoc on internal types as valid P3 and fixed by removal. The change adds this block, so this is not an older failure. P3 is the right severity.
